description: Per-shikigami/per-attack numeric tuning vectors read through GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue by character-specific action logic.

ID.simple: Unique tuning row ID (e.g. CN_010, CN_010_AttackA_01).
ID.technical: FName row key. AGameShikigami::ApplyCharacterSetup resolves every ShikigamiDataTable.Id_ShikigamiUnique[i] over ShikigamiUniqueDataTables (+0x700) into the UniqueRows array; the array index (RowIndex) is then used by consumers. Shikigami_FindRow skips None IDs (the shared finder rejects None), but a missing non-None row is added as null and a later read would be unchecked. 36 exported rows.

FloatValue.technical: TArray<float> (13 entries in every exported row). AGameShikigami::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(ValueIndex, RowIndex) returns UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] with no bounds checks (interface slot 155, retail 0x141482C80). The meaning of an index is per-character: e.g. CP_180 reads index 3 as boost-dash gauge cost and index 4 as per-second gauge drain from row 0; CP_270 reads index 1 of row 0 as an attack cancellation energy cost. The generic character status controller also uses these rows for gauge recovery/rate calculations keyed by effect type.

notes: ShikigamiUniqueDataTables is manager slot +0x700; the loader name is registered at GameDataTableManager.cpp:414 and resolved at line 242. ShikigamiVoiceGroupDataTables occupies the separate +0x6F0 slot.

There is no shared index-to-meaning map in the data: the same FloatValue slot has different meanings for different characters/actions. Consumers often annotate the index in comments; those annotations are the most specific evidence available.
The accessor is unchecked on both indices, so callers must supply a RowIndex present in Id_ShikigamiUnique and a ValueIndex within the array. Exported arrays are uniformly 13 floats.
Not to be confused with CharacterUniqueDataTable (per-character variants) or the character's own GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue path on AGameCharacter, which uses its own UniqueRows.

usages.detail: ApplyCharacterSetup resolves the Shikigami row's Id_ShikigamiUnique list into the shikigami's UniqueRows (retail 0x1485870).
GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(ValueIndex, RowIndex) performs the direct double-index array read (retail 0x141482C80).
CP_180 boost dash reads row 0 index 3 for normal-dash gauge cost and index 4 for drain rate.
CP_270 cancellation logic reads row 0 index 1 as an energy cost per cancelled attack.
Generic status rate calculations add FloatValue entries (indexes 0,1,2,4,8-derived) to recovery/scaling rates.
